scope: Static analysis of source mesh replacement and component-property refresh in the candidate mesh Split path; no native Split command executed.
observations: Candidate 0x14067cec0 obtains the source raw-mesh interface, saves a copy via 0x14067aa20, runs the candidate split helper and on success passes the output of 0x14033bc70 to the source object's pointer-replacement helper 0x14034aba0.

After the operation it invokes 0x14067a730. That helper accesses the UTF-16 name cSubMeshesProperty on the source object, clears a collection, traverses records from the source mesh, calls 0x14067a410 for newly labelled records, and stores the resulting count in the controller and mesh.

Candidate 0x14067aad0 replaces the source object's pointer with the saved copy and optionally calls the same property-refresh helper. Its role as an Undo or Cancel action is not proven from this code alone.
interpretation: The candidate route is consistent with one source object whose mesh is replaced and whose submesh property is refreshed. It does not independently establish UI-visible object inventory, exact component contents or Undo semantics.
validation: Ghidra decompiled the three helpers without whole-image auto-analysis under m2-split-native-history-static-20261028-r1-guard.json. Independent Capstone decoding covered all 173 Ghidra instruction starts, with one cmovz/cmove mnemonic alias. Both jobs used the 4 GiB guard and confirmed cleanup. Private Ghidra evidence SHA-256 583b16120875f6ad32fac47c3a330f7d23dd953a2ef2af897dc1d9c4de16c0cd.
limitations: Static function boundaries and inferred object types are not independently established.
The route has not been observed during a native Split on the prepared mesh fixtures.
No native facet counts, result ownership, save/reopen, selection, undo or GUI/MCP comparison was obtained.
